facts.statement: Datonglong was a herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur belonging to the Hadrosauroidea superfamily that lived in present-day China during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Datonglong is an extinct genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur, belonging to the Hadrosauroidea, which lived in the Late Cretaceous period in present-day China.

facts.statement: A team from the Shanxi Museum of Geological and Mineral Science and Technology discovered a euornithopod jaw in the Kangdailiang quarry in Shanxi in 2008.
facts.quote: In 2008, a team from the Shanxi Museum of Geological and Mineral Science and Technology in the Kangdailiang quarry in Shanxi discovered the jaw of a euornithopod.

facts.statement: The species Datonglong tianzhenensis was named and described in 2016 by Xu Shicha, You Hailu, Wang Jiawei, Wang Suozhu, Yi Jian, and Jia Lei.
facts.quote: In 2016, the species Datonglong tianzhenensis was named and described by Xu Shicha, You Hailu, Wang Jiawei, Wang Suozhu, Yi Jian, and Jia Lei.

facts.statement: The genus name Datonglong refers to the city of Datong and the Chinese word for dragon.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the city of Datong and the Chinese word long (龍), which means "dragon".

facts.statement: The specific name tianzhenensis refers to the fossil's origin in Tianzhen county.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to its origins in Tianzhen county.

facts.statement: Datonglong was one of eighteen dinosaur taxa described in 2015 in open access or free-to-read journals.
facts.quote: Datonglong was one of eighteen dinosaur taxa from 2015 to be described in open access or free-to-read journals.

facts.statement: The fossil was found within a layer of the Huiquanpu Formation.
facts.quote: The fossil was found in a layer of the Huiquanpu Formation.

facts.statement: The fossil is believed to date from the Cenomanian-Campanian timeframe, roughly between 95 and 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: Though the exact time the fossil was deposited is unknown, it is believed to date from somewhere in the Cenomanian-Campanian timeframe, roughly 95 to 80 million years ago.

facts.statement: Datonglong was established as a new genus due to its unique dental structures.
facts.quote: Datonglong was described as a new genus because of its unique dental structures.

facts.statement: The teeth are large, with intact teeth reaching up to 5.5 cm in height.
facts.quote: The teeth are large, standing up to 5.5 cm for a tooth not yet broken out.

facts.statement: The teeth are arranged in groups of three or four within the tooth battery.
facts.quote: Teeth stand in groups of three or four in the tooth battery.

facts.statement: Datonglong lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 99 and 71 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: el cual vivió a finales del período Cretácico, en algún momento entre 99 a 71 millones de años desde el Cenomaniense al Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Although the exact deposition time is unknown, the fossil is believed to be from the Cenomaniense to Campaniense epochs, approximately 95 to 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: Aunque se desconoce la época exacta en la que se halló el fósil, se cree que proviene de las épocas del Cenomaniense al Campaniense, hace aproximadamente entre 95 a 80 millones de años.

facts.statement: The time range for Datonglong is estimated from the Cenomanian to Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Campanian (100.5 to 72.2 million years ago)
